title: Time Needed to Rearrange a Binary String
statement:
`s` is a string made of the characters `'0'` and `'1'`. Every second, each place where a `'0'` is immediately followed by a `'1'` (a `"01"` pair) is turned into `"10"`, with all such pairs changed at the same moment based on the string as it was at the start of that second. This repeats until the string contains no `"01"` pair.

Return how many seconds pass before that happens (`0` if `s` has no `"01"` to begin with).
notes:
## Intuition

The rule is easy to apply directly: each second, scan the string and swap every `"01"` into `"10"`. The only subtlety is that the swaps must be simultaneous. Two `"01"` pairs can never overlap, but after swapping one pair the new `'0'` may sit right before an old `'1'` (from `"011"`). That new pair did not exist at the start of the second, so the scan must jump past a pair it just swapped. Each second moves at least one `'1'` left, and the process ends after fewer than `n` seconds, so for `n <= 1000` this direct simulation is fast enough.

## Approach

1. Copy `s` into an array `chars` so characters can be swapped; set `seconds = 0`.
2. Repeat a pass while the previous pass `changed` something.
3. In a pass, walk `i` from left to right. When `chars[i]` is `'0'` and `chars[i + 1]` is `'1'`, swap them, mark `changed`, and skip index `i + 1`.
4. If the pass swapped anything, one more second has passed.
5. When a pass finds no `"01"`, return `seconds`.

## Example 1, step by step

`s = "0110101"`.

- Pass 1 swaps at `i = 0`, skips to `i = 2`, swaps at `i = 3` and at `i = 5`: `"1011010"`, `seconds = 1`.
- Pass 2 gives `"1101100"`, pass 3 gives `"1110100"`, pass 4 gives `"1111000"`, so `seconds = 4`.
- Pass 5 finds no `"01"` and leaves `changed` false, so the answer is `4`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n²): each pass is O(n) and there are at most about n passes (for example `"000...111"`).
- Space: O(n) for the character array.
- Follow-up: an O(n) scan exists. For each `'1'`, with `zeros` zeros before it, its finishing time is `max(previous + 1, zeros)` when `zeros > 0`; the last such value is the answer.

## Pitfalls

- Without the `i++` skip, `"011"` would become `"110"` in one second instead of two, because the scan chains swaps that should happen in later seconds.
- Count a second only when the pass actually swapped something, or the final empty pass adds one too many.
- Strings are immutable in JavaScript, so swap inside an array, not on `s`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `chars` | the current string as an array of characters |
| `seconds` | how many seconds have passed |
| `changed` | whether the current pass swapped any `"01"` |
| `i` | position of the left character of the pair being checked |

narration.6: Keep simulating seconds while the last pass changed the string.
narration.7: Nothing has been swapped yet in this second.

narration.9: A '0' followed by a '1' is a pair that turns around this second.
narration.10: The '1' moves to the left position...
narration.12: Record that this second did something.
narration.13: Skip the character just swapped so the new '0' cannot pair with the next '1' in the same second.
narration.16: A pass that swapped anything counts as one second.
narration.20: No '01' remains, so the process is over.
